about.card1.body: An engine that can resolve fresh editions as often as daily, for every channel, for every surface a partner runs. A house of art directions we can tune or rebuild per brand. And a production process that gates every edition before it ships. The AI does the volume. Writers and showrunners decide what is good. Neither half works alone and we are not interested in pretending otherwise.
about.card1.head: What we built
about.card2.body: Writers, showrunners, game designers and AI engineers out of film, television and games. We move fast, we ship on schedule, and we hold a prestige bar on subject matter that most of this category does not bother with.
about.card2.head: Who is in the room
about.card3.body: Recurring games became some of the most valuable attention a brand or a publisher can own, while much of the industry was still calling them a nice-to-have. The gap is not creative and it is not technical. A game on a cadence is a standing production line, and almost nobody can run one, let alone several. We can, and we would rather run them under your brand than compete with you for the same audience.
about.card3.head: Why now
about.hero.h1: We make the thing you can’t staff.
about.intro.body: An AI games network that learns how to earn and sustain attention. We build premium games, distribute them through surfaces our partners already own, and connect what a player does back to the decision that produced it. That loop is the company. The games are how it learns.
about.intro.body2: Our founders come out of television, games and AI engineering. The television half matters more than it sounds. Procedural drama is the discipline of making self-contained stories on a schedule, at a quality bar that does not move, for years at a time. A vault of games on a cadence is the same job across several channels at once.
about.join.body: We are hiring writers, designers and engineers, and we are talking to partners about pilots.

legal.c3.body1: Play events answer one question: is this working, for this audience, this week. Every edition that runs teaches the next one what your audience actually finishes, so the vault gets sharper for them specifically. That is work we do on your behalf, continuously, and it is the part you would otherwise have to staff.
legal.c3.body2: Wolf Games is a network, and we are direct about what that means. Play data improves the platform across every deployment on it, which is why your vault benefits from work done on surfaces that are not yours. Play telemetry never enriches a third-party profile, is never sold, and is never joined to an advertising identity graph. Partner-identifying data is never exposed to another partner.
legal.c3.body3: The event log is the source of truth for both of us. You read the same events we read, which is the only way a retention number survives your own scrutiny.

pain.1.obs: Bought attention does not compound. Every campaign starts the audience from zero again.
pain.2.obs: A few seconds of passive view time is what most paid placements return, and it is the number under the most pressure internally.
pain.3.obs: The IP already performs. What is missing is a reason to open it on a Tuesday when nothing has launched.
pain.4.obs: Licensed catalog games are available, cheap, and instantly recognizable as somebody else’s product with a logo on it.
pain.5.obs: There is appetite for something like this at the top of the house, and no appetite for a two-year build to find out.
problem.cat.body1: The crossword, the horoscope, the Monday quiz. People do not schedule time for content, they schedule it for a ritual, and a ritual is the one thing in this business that still compounds. Most partners have already had the internal conversation about building one. It tends to stop in the same place. A game on a cadence is not a project, it is a standing production line, and almost nobody is staffed to run one on top of the work they already do. Nor should they be.

problem.mech.body: A licensed catalog game is a stock puzzle wearing your colors, and your audience can tell inside ten seconds. We start from the other end. What your audience already does with you becomes the thing they do in the game.

problem.mech.h2a: Anyone can put your logo on a puzzle.

problem.mech.p1.body: An investigation brand gets a game about searching a scene and assembling the case. A food brand gets a board that fills with the product and pays out in real rewards. A sports brand gets a game played against the clock and the table. The verb of the game is your verb.
problem.mech.p1.head: The mechanic comes from what you do.
problem.mech.p2.body: Your catalog, your cast, your world, your back issues, your library, your product line. It is the one asset in this business nobody can license out from under you, and it was built to do one job. It can carry another.
problem.mech.p2.head: The content comes from what you own.
problem.mech.p3.body: Every channel is fronted by a character with a history and a way of seeing the world. Your on-air talent, your mascot, or someone we build with you. People come back for a person, not a mechanic.
problem.mech.p3.head: The host comes from who you are.
problem.mech.p4.body: We keep a house of styles to move fast, and we build bespoke ones when the identity demands it. Nothing ships that would look at home on somebody else’s surface.
problem.mech.p4.head: The art direction is yours.
problem.now.body1: Search is becoming an answer surface rather than a referral engine. When an AI summary appears, people click a traditional result on 8 percent of visits, against 15 percent when it does not, and only 1 percent click a source cited inside the summary. Across more than 2,500 sites, Google organic referrals fell 33 percent in a single year, and publishers surveyed expect another 43 percent decline over the next three.
problem.now.body2: Nobody is coming back through the front door the way they used to. Direct habit is what is left, and it is worth more than it has ever been worth.
problem.now.h2: The audience is still there. The road to them is closing.

stance.expect.2: We expect a game built out of your world to pull harder than a licensed catalog identical on a hundred other surfaces.
stance.expect.3: We expect a set of channels to hold a broader share of your audience than any single mechanic can.
stance.expect.4: We expect an audience that plays several times a week to be worth materially more to you than one that arrives once from a link.
